correctness.rationale: CND is equivalent to all nontrivial central Fourier eigenvalues being nonpositive. The Jucys content formula yields every one, with exact multiplicity. The shape (n-2,1,1) has polynomial (1-z)(1-2z)prod(1+jz); a one-sign-change fractional integral proves one root in (0,1), monotone in n. Direct uniform estimates at 100/(n-3)! yield the factorial upper bound for n>=53. Exact Fraction interval checks isolate beta_6 and bound every competing Young-sector eigenvalue strictly below zero; hook lengths give multiplicity 100 and Euclidean rank 619. A supplementary exhaustive 720-point matrix reconstruction independently confirms the finite spectrum. No extrapolation from finite checks is used for all n.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact CND powered-distance statement and its equivalent generalized-roundness and reflection-length formulations, rather than only matching titles. Jucys–Murphy content diagonalization, general negative-type interval properties, Cayley graph automorphisms and adjacency spectra are credited. New signed-integral comparisons, a strictly decreasing factorial obstruction, and all-sector exact six-letter critical equality do not follow from the inspected sources. Search-based originality is provisional, with residual risk explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: Earlier non-English or non-indexed group-metric literature might contain the same six-letter numerical threshold or a stronger reflection-length generalized-roundness estimate.
Source-index search results on the three closely related public records were compared at title/summary level; their full papers were not claimed inspected.

value.rationale: Generalized roundness of a canonical group-invariant shortest-path metric is a natural Hilbert-embedding and positive-definite-kernel invariant. A sharp 720-point critical exponent with a single 100-dimensional irreducible obstruction, plus a universal factorial decay upper bound, gives structural new information beyond adjacency spectra and standalone numerics. It bounds but does not identify larger-rank thresholds.
